title: Emergent VibeCon SF (Oct 24-25) Winners: Manceps Takes $10K and a Direct YC Interview
summary: VibeCon SF 2026 winners are here: Manceps takes $10K and a YC interview, with Floorline and Kazza as runners-up. See what each team built on Emergent.
body_markdown:
Manceps, an AI dispatcher for trucking companies, has won VibeCon SF 2026. The team took home $10,000 and a direct interview with Y Combinator for an upcoming batch. Floorline won the runner-up spot and $5,000, and Kazza placed third with $3,000.


All three products were built from scratch on Emergent over two days. The event rules required every project to be built during the competition, with the Emergent Agent writing all the code.


## What VibeCon SF 2026 was


[VibeCon](https://vibecon.com/) brought builders together in San Francisco on October 24 and 25, 2026. An expert panel picked participants from open applications, and they competed solo or in teams of up to three. Emergent hosted the event, MongoDB powered it, and AWS and Anthropic's Claude were supporting partners.


Read the full format in our[VibeCon SF announcement](https://emergent.sh/news/vibecon-sf-oct-24-25-build-ship-win-10k-yc) .


The judging panel:


- **Nicolas Dessaigne:** General Partner, Y Combinator
- **Sachin Malhotra:** Member of Technical Staff, Anthropic
- **Balaji NJL:** Senior Solutions Architect, AWS
- **Pratik Gupta:** Senior Engineering Leader, Stripe
- **Mukund Jha:** CEO, Emergent
- **Madhav Jha:** CTO, Emergent


## Meet the VibeCon SF 2026 winners


### 1. Manceps (winner): an AI dispatcher for trucking fleets


Built by[Aryan Daga](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aryandaga/) , co-founder and CTO of Morphiq Labs, and[Yeabsira Teshome](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yeabsira-teshome-1708222b1/) .


Manceps hands a dispatcher's daily work to an[AI agent](https://emergent.sh/ai-agent-builder) that acts on its own. In the live demo, it called a driver for an ETA, confirmed the next pickup, and then called brokers to find a return load so the truck wouldn't come back empty. Operators can also set the agent to negotiate rates on their behalf.


**Prize:** $10,000 and a direct YC interview.


### 2. Floorline (1st runner-up): AI pricing for small furniture stores


Built solo by[Nikhil Marudai](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikhil-marudai-23b128177/) , who deferred his medical school admission to build in AI and is the co-founder of Organism, an AI co-scientist for single-cell biology.


Floorline was built for a real family-run furniture store near Sacramento that priced every item by hand. The owner sets her pricing rules once, and every item gets a minimum price that salespeople can't go below. A visual floor map shows how long each piece has been sitting, and the owner can ask plain-English questions about what sells. Plans start at $200 a month.


**Prize:** $5,000.


### 3. Kazza (2nd runner-up): an AI architect for California lots


Built solo by[Bruno Rodríguez](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bruno-rodriguez-sepulveda) , founding engineer at Breezy, which builds AI for real estate agents.


Kazza turns a lot, a building type, and one sentence into a room-by-room floor plan. It then checks each room against 39 rules from California ADU law and the residential code, citing the code for every finding. The AI never approves its own work, and a licensed professional confirms every finding. The same model produces drawing sets, a 3D walkthrough, a cost estimate, and BIM and CAD exports for small architecture firms designing ADUs.


**Prize:** $3,000.


## What's next for the winners


Manceps now heads into its YC interview. Floorline and Kazza leave VibeCon with working products, each aimed at a specific group of[small businesses](https://emergent.sh/solutions/smb-owners) .


Congratulations to all three teams, and thank you to every builder who made VibeCon SF 2026 a weekend to remember. If you'd like to compete next time, keep watching this space for the next VibeCon announcement and other[AI contests](https://emergent.sh/ai-contests) organized by Emergent.
